text:
Samir Patel: Quick check-in — seeing tenant priority buckets (QoS) vanish from leases after pool scale events. Not sure if this is operator or admission path. Anyone noticed?

Jing Wu: Yup saw that on staging this morning. Pod got bounced and the lease annotation that carries priority ended up missing. Looks like the operator reconcile doesn't always persist the admission token metadata.

Kevin Morales: I ran a short trace — operator reads priority at admission and only keeps it ephemeral in memory; when we reassign shards we re-create leases without rehydrating that field.

Anya Kuznetsova: Oof. Two ways to approach: (A) make priority canonical in the Lease CRD (persisted field) so any controller/operator can read it; (B) keep it ephemeral but add a stronger handshake so re-create path copies from admission store.

Samir Patel: Tradeoff: (A) is clearer/safe but requires migration + bumping CRD and operator contract. (B) cheaper short term but brittle. We also need to think about how this interacts with preemption: losing priority causes tenants to be treated as best-effort.

Jing Wu: For short-term I propose operator writes an annotation rwd.priority_bucket onto Lease before attaching to node, and backfill existing leases in a background job. That gets us safety quickly.

Kevin Morales: Agreed. One gotcha: attach sequence -> if we write annotation after node attach scheduler may have already done allocation decisions. We should write annotation atomically ahead of attach. Using optimistic update (compare resourceVersion) should be fine.

Anya Kuznetsova: Also worry about drift — if we have two places that own the same information (admission token store + Lease spec) we'll need a canonical source and clear upgrade path. If we make Lease the source, admission becomes best-effort writer and operator must enforce.

Samir Patel: Plan sketch: 1) hotfix: operator writes rwd.priority_bucket annotation on lease pre-attach + background backfill job. 2) followup RFC to add PriorityBucket string to Lease.spec and guarantee operator will never drop it. 3) migration: operator backfills and marks a feature-gate for a grace window before we rely on spec.

Jing Wu: I'll help with tests — need unit tests for reconcile (create/update) and an e2e that simulates scale-down/scale-up and ensures priority survives. Also add an alert: if >0 leases without rwd.priority_bucket after attach, fire a warning.

Kevin Morales: Quick pseudo patch for reconcile (happy-path):
```go
// controller reconcile snippet (pseudo)
if lease.Annotations["rwd.priority_bucket"] == "" {
    lease.Annotations["rwd.priority_bucket"] = admission.Token.PriorityBucket
    if err := client.Update(ctx, lease); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("persist priority annotation: %w", err)
    }
}
// then proceed to attach to node
```

Anya Kuznetsova: :thumbsup: make sure update is before we mutate attach fields. Also add a histogram metric for "lease.annotation_missing_total" and a small alert threshold.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: operator/lease-propagation v2 canary rolled to staging (tag: lease-prop-v2-canary).

Samir Patel: Nice. I'll draft the RFC for the Lease-spec change and include the migration plan + test matrix. Ping me if you want sections assigned.

Jing Wu: Pinged. I'll own e2e tests and the backfill job.

Kevin Morales: I'll prototype the reconcile change and a small concurrency test.

Anya Kuznetsova: I'll write the metrics/alert PR and add the feature-gate config.

Samir Patel: Great — thanks all. Follow-up in thread when RFC is up. :rocket:
